task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing and input preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink or fetch call.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: DOM CustomEvent on the main document

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle and no source map is exposed to the agent.
The target field name is assembled from adjusted character-code arrays at the sink, so direct literal search is insufficient.
The target property code is carried through runtime-derived transport keys and recovered shortly before console output and fetch submission.
The encode route selects its live configuration only after click-time DOM, form-order, style and dataset state are captured.

The click path crosses delegated event handling, action routing, gate checks, property collection with PII scrubbing and key-order normalization, tuple construction, asynchronous scheduling, local event dispatch, middleware pipeline, runtime slot materialization, state encoding and sink wrapping.
The same encode interaction emits non-target analytics-like objects carrying props_code-like values before the target analytics.properties object.
A telemetry.props shadow emitter logs a ctx-styled fake frame via console.debug, and an inactive audit chain remains reachable-looking without feeding the target props_code field.
The target value is separated from the click by Promise, microtask, timer, animation-frame, MutationObserver and DOM CustomEvent boundaries.
The selected runtime configuration is cloned and mutated in a WeakMap-backed materialization step before the encoder receives it.
The code passes through a queue push and drain before the fetch body and console emission, so sink inspection alone does not identify the construction site.

behavior_category.subtype: PII-scrubbed, order-normalized property entries folded into a 12-char base36 state code
behavior_category.reason: The observable value is a compact deterministic encoding of normalized property state, scope selection, tuple shape and runtime machine state. The primary observation target is the locally computed state code itself; the fetch to the props collect endpoint is a mirror outlet whose body reuses the same value, so the value semantics do not change with transport. It is not a request signature, byte-array payload, browser fingerprint or request-body rewrite.

near_categories.why_not: The primary observable is a local state code; the fetch is a mirror outlet and the value semantics do not change with transport.
The 12-char code is an encoding of normalized property state that the receiving end can decode and verify; it is not a one-way digest or seal.
The chain uses local DOM/form state and page context, not browser/device capability collection as the target behavior.
